headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: ComfyUI is offline/local, while Taipy has no exposed I/O surfaces or network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can ingest files and workflows, so malicious content could be manually bridged into Taipy, but neither profile shows a shared channel or default direct ingestion. Taipy exposes no I/O surfaces, and ComfyUI is offline by default, so the pathway is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies ComfyUI-generated workflow text into Taipy inputs
IF Taipy is configured to parse untrusted text as instructions
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Treat ComfyUI outputs as data, not instructions
Add a manual review step before reuse
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model files, but its network egress is vendor-only and it can run fully offline. Taipy shows no data classes touched and no I/O surfaces, so there is no documented default path for sensitive data to leak across the pair.
conditions: IF sensitive assets are placed in ComfyUI's model or workflow files
IF Taipy is later connected to the same workspace or storage
mitigations: Store sensitive assets outside shared folders
Review ComfyUI workflow exports before sharing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and Taipy exposes no write or mutable-resource capabilities in the profile. With no overlapping write surface, a capability conflict pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF Taipy is extended with write access to the same directory as ComfyUI
IF an external orchestrator grants both agents shared mutable state
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible
requires-engineering: add locking for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can produce workflows and assets that Taipy might consume, but Taipy is not runnable and has no documented action-taking authority here. Without evidence that Taipy treats ComfyUI output as authoritative, the cascade is limited and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF Taipy is used to ingest ComfyUI-generated artifacts without validation
IF downstream automation is added to Taipy
mitigations: Require human approval for downstream steps
Keep Taipy from auto-executing imported artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles: both are open-source, docs-only, and no residency, certification, retention, or PHI handling claims are present. Because the profiles do not assert a regulated-data pathway, a compliance breach is not supported.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent
IF deployment policies impose residency or retention constraints not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair
